vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: beautsgo-booking
Version: 1.0.3

The skill bundle is a legitimate assistant for booking Korean beauty services via the BeautsGO platform. The code logic in 'api/skill.js' and 'api/browser/open-url.js' aligns with the stated purpose of matching hospital names, providing booking guides, and submitting appointment requests to a specific API (api.yestokr.com). While 'open-url.js' utilizes 'child_process.exec' to open the system browser (a high-risk capability), it implements a strict hostname whitelist ('i.beautsgo.com') and protocol validation to prevent arbitrary command injection. No evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized persistence, or malicious prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions mostly match its stated purpose (booking via BeautsGO), but there are a couple of inconsistencies — most notably an external API hostname that doesn't match the BeautsGO domain and a pre-scan prompt-injection signal — that warrant caution before install.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, network permissions (i.beautsgo.com + a single POST endpoint), and included code/data (hospitals.json, rendering/matching logic) align with a BeautsGO booking helper. No unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and code restrict browser openings to the BeautsGO subdomain and only send booking payloads to a single API endpoint when the user provides contact info. This is within scope. However, SKILL.md and code state the booking POST goes to https://api.yestokr.com/api/Appointment/saveFromSkill — that API host is different from the BeautsGO domain used elsewhere; the skill claims no data storage, but it will transmit user phone numbers to that external endpoint when booking. Also a pre-scan found unicode-control-chars in SKILL.md (possible prompt-injection artifact) — investigate before trusting the instructions verbatim.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote binary downloads or obscure install steps. The package is a Node skill with an npm dependency (pinyin-pro) and standard npm install usage. No install script pulls arbitrary archives or external installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The only sensitive action is sending user-provided contact info (phone number) to the booking API; that behavior is proportional to a booking skill but depends on whether the API host is trusted. No other secrets or unrelated config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills, and is not asking for persistent elevated privileges. It reads a bundled local hospitals.json dataset and does not persist user data in code (privacy claims that user data is only sent on explicit consent).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a legitimate BeautsGO booking helper and contains the local hospital database and rendering/matching code. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the booking API host (api.yestokr.com) — confirm it is an official BeautsGO API (or authorized partner). The skill will POST user phone numbers to that endpoint when you ask it to book. 2) Inspect SKILL.md for hidden/control characters (scanner flagged unicode-control-chars) and confirm the consent flow is enforced — make sure the agent asks you explicitly before sending contact info. 3) Note that open-url executes shell commands to launch the system browser, but the code enforces a whitelist (i.beautsgo.com). 4) If you need higher assurance, ask the maintainer for proof that api.yestokr.com is owned/operated by BeautsGO (or switch bookings to a verified endpoint). Given the domain mismatch and the prompt-injection signal, proceed only after verifying the API domain and the consent behavior.
llm.findings: [unicode-control-chars] unexpected: Scanner detected unicode control characters in SKILL.md which can be used to hide or obfuscate text (prompt-injection technique). This is not expected for a straightforward booking guide; review SKILL.md for hidden characters before trusting its instructions.
